This research investigates how pedagogical content knowledge influences the instructional decisions of biology teachers when implementing an inquiry approach.

Ricardo T. Bagarinao has advised three theses in this repository between 2021 and 2026. Their research focus spans several distinct areas including governance and public policy, climate and disaster, communication studies, management and leadership, environment and sustainability, teacher training, instructional design, and science education. Based on the items available in this repository, they have supervised work that examines localized communication strategies and their impact on household disaster preparedness in flood-prone areas like Barangay Commonwealth in Quezon City. This work is grounded in the Risk Perception and Communication Model and touches upon themes of community resilience and disaster awareness. Another area of their supervision involves comparative studies of laws and policies, specifically regarding plastic waste management practices in Indonesia and the Philippines. This research addresses issues related to the circular economy, policy regulation, and the environmental impacts of urbanization and growing populations in archipelagic nations. Additionally, they have supervised research into science education, specifically focusing on biology teachers. This work investigates pedagogical content knowledge and decision-making processes when implementing inquiry-based approaches in classroom settings.
